Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberFortress Inc. Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberFortress Inc.'s results for the second quarter fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer, and Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. CyberFortress had an exceptional Q2, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. We are seeing significant traction with our cloud-native security platform and are benefiting from the increased focus on cybersecurity across all industries. The impact of our new AI-powered threat detection is evident in the reduced incident response times reported by our customers.

Our strategy is centered around five core pillars: advancing the performance of our key product lines like cloud security and SASE, driving new customer acquisition, issuing confident next-quarter billings guidance, making strong progress on key strategic initiatives, and capitalizing on favorable market share trends.

Today, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our progress across our four cornerstone strategic initiatives: accelerating our Zero Trust platform adoption, embedding generative AI into our XDR ecosystem, expanding our footprint in high-growth regions, and executing on our M&A pipeline to bolster endpoint and identity capabilities. These initiatives are not just checkboxes—they're driving our revenue growth, with annual recurring revenue now exceeding levels that reflect robust expansion.

First, on Zero Trust Architecture acceleration. We've seen explosive demand as enterprises pivot from legacy VPNs amid rising nation-state threats and supply chain vulnerabilities. Our CyberFortress Zero platform, which integrates SASE with continuous adaptive trust, now powers thousands of customers with significant increases quarter-over-quarter. Key wins include major financial services firms migrating tens of thousands of users, contributing substantial new annual contract value. Adoption metrics are stellar: average deployment time has dropped significantly thanks to our automated policy orchestration engine. Net revenue retention from Zero Trust cohorts is strong, reflecting upsell to micro-segmentation add-ons that reduce lateral movement risks in customer proofs-of-concept. We're on track to capture meaningful market share in the SASE space, outpacing peers.

Shifting to AI/ML integration in our Extended Detection and Response suite. With ransomware attacks surging, our GenAI-powered Sentinel has become a game-changer. We've deployed autonomous threat hunting across a majority of our customer base, dramatically reducing mean time to respond, validated by independent evaluations where we score high on zero-day detection. This drove a significant portion of bookings, including multi-year deals with major telcos. R&D investment remains robust, fueling innovations like NLP-driven deception grids with lower false positives via advanced learning techniques. Customer feedback shows strong plans to expand AI workloads, positioning us for high growth in XDR.

On regional expansion, we're capitalizing on global cyber maturity differences. North America remains our powerhouse, fueled by federal mandates—securing contracts with top defense contractors. EMEA has accelerated with compliance directives; our data centers now serve hundreds of customers with sovereignty features boosting win rates. APAC is rising fast, with landmark deals underscoring our compliant stack, outmaneuvering competitors. International revenue mix has expanded, diversifying us beyond U.S. hyperscalers. Latin America pilots are converting well.

Finally, M&A and partnerships to supercharge endpoint and identity. We closed a major acquisition integrating EDR capabilities into our stack, adding net-new logos and run-rate ARR, with cross-sell velocity strong. Synergies are materializing in improved detection times. Partnerships with hyperscalers generated significant bookings, while identity federations serve joint customers. We're eyeing more tuck-ins for OT/IoT security.

These initiatives are delivering outstanding performance. Looking ahead, our cash position gives us dry powder for continued execution.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we had a remarkable Q2. Revenue reached $420 million, reflecting a 45% year-over-year increase. This growth was fueled by both new customer acquisition and expansion within our existing customer base. Our gross margin remained strong at 80%, demonstrating our ability to scale efficiently. Operating expenses were $250 million, and net income was $90 million, translating to $0.75 per share. We are increasing our guidance for the full year based on these outstanding results.

I'm thrilled with the momentum we're seeing across our portfolio, particularly in our core growth engines: Cloud Security and SASE. These product lines now represent a significant portion of our total ARR, underscoring our leadership in cloud-native protection and secure edge networking.

Starting with Cloud Security, which delivered $178 million in Q2 revenue—that's 52% year-over-year growth and 14% quarter-over-quarter. This segment, encompassing our Cloud Native Application Protection Platform, Cloud Access Security Broker, and Cloud Security Posture Management offerings, continues to outperform the broader market. We're positioned as a Leader in Gartner's latest Magic Quadrant for Security Service Edge for the third consecutive year, and our CNAPP suite—powered by our proprietary Nebula Engine for runtime behavioral analytics—captured strong market share in cloud workload protection, edging out competitors.

Key drivers include a surge in multi-cloud adoption, where misconfigurations account for a high percentage of breaches per our latest Threat Landscape Report. We saw substantial ARR expansion, fueled by hundreds of net new logos, including major wins at Fortune 500 financials like a top-tier U.S. bank migrating tens of thousands of workloads. Our net revenue retention hit record highs thanks to upsells in data security posture management, where we integrated AI-driven discovery for shadow SaaS apps, reducing mean time to detect significantly in trials.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, up strongly on regulatory tailwinds like SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules. APAC exploded with hyperscaler partnerships, where we're embedding CSPM as a managed service. EMEA grew solidly, with localized sovereign cloud compliance features.

Strategically, we're doubling down on agentless CWPP innovations, like Nebula Fusion, which unifies vulnerability management with container runtime security using advanced telemetry. This positions us ahead in zero-trust workload segmentation, with pilots secured across large enterprises.

Now, turning to SASE, our fastest-growing line at $142 million in Q2 revenue—a 68% YoY increase and 18% QoQ. SASE, blending our SD-WAN fabric, Zero Trust Network Access, Secure Web Gateway, and Firewall-as-a-Service into a single cloud-delivered stack, is riding hybrid work and branch consolidation waves. We're outpacing the market in ZTNA.

ARR here surged significantly, with gross margin expansion from optimized global points of presence. Customer highlights include multi-year deals displacing legacy VPNs and expansions leveraging DLP-infused SWG against ransomware.

Trends show a shift to greenfield zero-trust implementations as enterprises ditch perimeter models post major breaches. Our net retention is stellar, driven by convergence plays boosting average ACV.

Geographically, APAC led with partnerships like co-branded appliances. North America and EMEA grew robustly, with LatAm emerging.

On the technical front, we launched SASE 3.0 with ML-powered adaptive trust using graph neural networks, slashing false positives. We're advancing SSE convergence with identity integrations.

Looking ahead, we expect strong growth in these lines, with cross-sell driving bookings. Macro tailwinds like nation-state threats accelerate adoption. These product lines are redefining cybersecurity economics.

As we dive into operational metrics, I'd like to start with new customer acquisitions. In Q2, we added 452 new customers to our platform, marking a 38% year-over-year increase from last year and 16% sequential uplift. This underscores accelerating momentum in our go-to-market amid a volatile landscape.

The cohort broke down into 128 enterprise logos over $1 million ARR, 212 mid-market, and 112 SMBs. This reflects our land-and-expand strategy, prioritizing high-value enterprises while scaling via channels. Enterprise win rate improved to 42%, driven by displacing legacy solutions in XDR evaluations.

Key drivers tie to our CyberFortress Nexus platform, an AI-native SASE integrating ZTNA, SWG, and CASB, reducing deployment times versus competitors. Traction in financial services and healthcare neutralizes APTs like ransomware variants.

Regionally, North America accounted for 62% or 280 customers, fueled by SEC rules and hyperscaler integrations. EMEA added 105, up 32% with NIS2 compliance. APAC 67, up 55% with partnerships.

Strategically, product-led innovation like GenAI defenses with autonomous SOAR cuts MTTR. Ecosystem expansion saw channel bookings at 52%. Vertical specialization into OT-IIoT netted wins.

We expect acceleration into Q3 targeting 500+ logos.

I'd also like to spend a few minutes on our market share trends, which continue to underscore our platform-led strategy. The global cybersecurity market is growing rapidly, fueled by ransomware, APTs, and gen-AI phishing. Within EDR/XDR, we're expanding via our integrated SecureXDR platform.

Globally, our share in core segments stood at 11.2% at quarter-end, up from prior periods, with sequential gains driven by ARR increases. In EDR, we've climbed to 10.1%, bolstered by low-latency agents trained on massive signals. We displaced incumbents in 42% of deals.

Segment-specific: Endpoint/XDR share rose to 10.1%, outpacing growth with GenAI analytics reducing false positives. We've won major migrations. CWPP/CNAPP share to 9.7% via runtime protection. SASE/ZTNA at 8.9%, with high win rates.

These gains stem from heavy R&D into cloud-native security and quantum-resistant encryption.

Regionally: North America 14.5% share, propelled by federal wins. EMEA 9.8%, turbocharged by NIS2. APAC 15.2% amid state attacks. LATAM doubling.

Our platform convergence bet is validated, with high multi-module adoption. Cash funds M&A to accelerate.

Risks like hyperscaler bundling are offset by our neutrality.

We target further share through growth in key regions.

As we wrap up Q2 with strong billings, I'm excited to share our outlook for Q3. We're guiding billings to $485 million to $505 million, representing 28% to 32% year-over-year growth at the midpoint and 7% to 12% sequential. This embeds confidence amid geopolitical tensions, GenAI phishing, and regulations.

Core subscription billings grow 30%, fueled by multi-year deals. Strength in Next-Gen Endpoint Protection integrated with XDR.

SASE and CWP accelerating, with quantum-resistant features positioning us ahead. Consumption adds incrementally.

Regionally, Americas ~60%, EMEA pacing well, APAC fastest.

We're investing in AI Sentinel driving logos, outcome-based pricing lifting expansion.

Guidance incorporates sales cycle conservatism and churn risks, with upside from launches.

This reflects robust execution.

Next, Taylor Kim will provide more technical details.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. We continue to innovate and push the boundaries of what's possible in cybersecurity. Our team is focused on developing cutting-edge solutions that address the evolving threat landscape. We are investing heavily in research and development to stay ahead of the curve and deliver unparalleled value to our customers. Key areas of focus include advancing our Nebula Engine for behavioral analytics, Nebula Fusion for unified vulnerability and runtime security, ML-powered adaptive trust in SASE 3.0 with graph neural networks, GenAI defenses like autonomous SOAR, and Vanguard AI Sentinel for high true positive rates on threat evaluations. These innovations, including eBPF telemetry, quantum-resistant encryption, and federated learning for low false positives, ensure we're neutralizing advanced threats like zero-days and ransomware in real-time across cloud, endpoint, network, and identity.

Morgan Patel: Thank you. Cybersecurity is paramount, and we are taking proactive measures to protect our customers and ourselves. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance, with features like data sovereignty, GDPR-aligned DLP, PDPA-compliant stacks, and CMMC readiness ensuring resilience against nation-state actors, supply chain attacks, and regulatory scrutiny.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the question and answer session. First question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks for taking my question. Can you elaborate on the competitive dynamics in cloud security and SASE, especially with recent wins against Prisma Cloud and Zscaler?

Alex Rivera: Great question, John. Our leadership in Gartner's Magic Quadrant and IDC share metrics reflect our edge. In cloud security, Nebula Engine's runtime analytics and agentless CWPP like Nebula Fusion give us advantages in multi-cloud sprawl and zero-trust segmentation, as seen in our Fortune 500 bank migrations and 128% NRR. For SASE, SASE 3.0's adaptive trust and 180 PoPs enable faster deployments and higher ACV, displacing VPNs in deals like the European telco. We've blocked billions of zero-days YTD, outpacing competitors in MTTD/MTTR.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen: Jordan, on the new customer adds and billings guide—how does the 452 logos and Q3 range factor into full-year expectations amid macro uncertainty?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Emily. The 452 adds, with 38% YoY growth and strong enterprise mix, validate our Nexus traction and channel ramp to 52%. Q3 billings at $485-505M build on Q2's 36% growth, with RPO at record levels and 118% expansion. We've baked in sales cycle conservatism but see upside from SASE/CWP ramps and GSPM launch. Full-year remains 30%+ trajectory.

Operator: Next question comes from David Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

David Rodriguez: Taylor, curious about the AI integrations—how are they performing in MITRE evals versus CrowdStrike or Palo Alto?

Taylor Kim: David, our GenAI Sentinel and XDR score 92-98% on MITRE ATT&CK for zero-days, with 70% false positive reductions via graph networks and federated learning. Customers see MTTR under 5 minutes, driving 22% of bookings. We're ahead in behavioral anomaly detection, resonating in RFPs.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays.

Lisa Wong: Alex, on market share and strategic initiatives—any updates on M&A or regional expansion plans?

Alex Rivera: Lisa, share gains to 11.2% globally, with APAC at 15.2%, stem from platform convergence and R&D. Initiatives like EnduraSec integration added $150M ARR and 60% cross-sell. Regional mix to 42% international, with Q3 tuck-ins eyed for OT/IoT. $2.1B cash positions us for $100M+ logos.

Alex Rivera: Thank you all for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. Thank you to our dedicated employees, loyal customers, and valued partners.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
